subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Does the candidate's stable protected-tool catalogue plus immutable pre-execution ToolAccessPolicy preserve the intended authorization boundary for owner, trusted-internal, non-owner, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns?
rationale: Source and live proof support the cache fix, but deciding whether protected capability schemas may remain model-visible while execution is denied is an intentional security-boundary choice that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the split boundary
options.body: Accept stable schema visibility with complete current-turn policy snapshots and mandatory denial before hooks, implementations, or side effects.

options.title: Require narrower visibility
options.body: Request a different stable catalogue or disclosure model while preserving deterministic prompt shape and pre-execution enforcement.

options.title: Pause the candidate
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until security owners define a replacement visibility-versus-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the split boundary
recommendation.body: Accept stable schema visibility with complete current-turn policy snapshots and mandatory denial before hooks, implementations, or side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: This team owns the repository's security-sensitive authorization review and is the best available decision owner for the capability boundary.
